key_insight: Non-dimensionalization can determine PINN trainability: free-fall scaling limits buoyancy-driven gradient imbalance that undermines thermal-diffusive scaling.
engineering_relevance: Choosing physically appropriate scaling can improve PINN predictions of buoyancy-driven heat transfer without changing the training setup.
method: Compare thermal-diffusive and free-fall scalings under identical training conditions.
Evaluate differentially heated square-cavity flow at Pr = 0.71 and Ra = 10³–10⁵.
Measure loss gradients and test sparse-data supervision and adaptive loss weighting.
evidence_signal: For Ra ≤ 10⁴, free-fall scaling yields mean Nusselt-number errors below 1.1%, versus 157–650% for thermal-diffusive scaling, which diverges at Ra = 10⁵.
watch_item: Free-fall scaling still misses the transient Nusselt-number overshoot in unsteady convection despite accurate long-time heat transfer.
paper_title: Inherent Failure Modes of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Buoyancy-Driven Flow: Role of Non-Dimensionalization in Network Training
